problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x+3,\,y(0)=0
$$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =(x{y}^{′}+{y}^{′})\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+3x,$ compute the local truncation error, ${τ}_{1},$ for the first step starting at $x=0$ with step size $Δx=0.1.$

${τ}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact $y$-value at the start of the step $x=0$ is $y(0)=0.$ Now, let's compute the 
$y$-increment using the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(0) & =2(0)+3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =(x\cdot {y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(0)+{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(0))\cdot Δx \\  & =(0\cdot 3+3)\cdot 0.1 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0+0.1) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.1) \\  & =(0.1)^{2}+3(0.1) \\  & =0.01+0.3 \\  & =0.31.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the first step starting at $x=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{1} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-(y(0)+Δy) \\  & =0.31-(0+0.3) \\  & =0.01\end{aligned}
$$
